stemMd: Which practice best embodies the passage's approach?

options.label: A
options.textMd: A judge lists similarities but never explains their relevance.

options.label: B
options.textMd: A judge treats sophistication alone as decisive without reading the earlier reasons.

options.label: C
options.textMd: A judge explains why the earlier concern about meaningful choice applies to a sophisticated firm lacking alternative suppliers.

options.label: D
options.textMd: A judge says every factual difference defeats precedent.

options.label: E
options.textMd: A judge declares precedent binding only when names and dates match.

explanationMd: The practice identifies the operative reason and shows why it can apply despite a difference in experience. It makes the comparison explicit rather than assuming that superficial similarity or difference settles the case.

distractorRationale.b: That skips the relevant interpretive bridge.
distractorRationale.a: A list does not connect facts to reasons.
distractorRationale.d: The passage requires distinguishing relevant from irrelevant differences.
